Definition: middle voice from G1537 and G3004 (in its primary sense); to select:--make choice, choose (out), chosen.
BiblicalUsage: To choose is to select, and the New Testament says God does the choosing before we do. Jesus says, Have not I chosen you twelve, and, Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and Paul says God chose us in Him before the foundation of the world. The apostles pray for God to show which of two men He has chosen to take Judas's place, because the choice is His to make.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe election is the comfort of my faith, because I did not choose God first; He chose me, and His choice does not change. My position is that being chosen makes me secure, not proud, because the choice was grace from the start.
